utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Will the Registrar call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Case number IT-00-39 & 40-PT, the Prosecutor versus Biljana Plavsic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: The appearances.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. President and Your Honours. My name is Mark Harmon. Assisting me is my co-counsel, Mr. Alan Tieger.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Harmon, where were you when we were due to begin? We've all been waiting for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I apologise. I was in a meeting with representatives of the Dutch government, and then I was in a meeting with Mr. Boas, and then I had to finish that meeting and get my robe. So I apologise for delaying the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. Yes. For the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVICH
utterances.text: On behalf of Ms. Biljana Plavsic, Robert Pavich. I'm assisted by Eugene O'Sullivan.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. And for the Dutch government.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE MAN
utterances.text: We have two representatives of the Ministry of Justice, Mr. Abraham Visser and Mr. Jan van den Heuvel, and two representatives of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Mr. Niels Blokker and I myself am Frederique de Man.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Thank you. This hearing is in open session. If at any stage any of the parties or indeed the government wish the matter to go into closed session, they can make an application. The Trial Chamber is holding this hearing in relation to an application for provisional release by Mrs. Plavsic. It was made by way of motion filed on the 11th of July. The Prosecutor responded on the 25th of July, and the Prosecutor's position is this: that there is no objection, as I understand it, to provisional release provided, that is, that various conditions are met. And, Mr. Harmon, it seems to me that -- those conditions which bring us here today are matters which in the outset can be dealt with in open session. Have you any objections to dealing with them in open session? At least to deal with the presence of the government here. There may, of course, be matters of detail which should be dealt with in private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Insofar as the conditions themselves that have been suggested by the Office of the Prosecutor, I have no objection to those being identified, but once we get into the details, I will be making a motion for a closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. The condition which is pertinent is this: that the accused should remain on the territory of the Netherlands. The Trial Chamber, on receiving that response from the Office of the Prosecutor, invited the government to respond, which they did very promptly, and they have sought clarification of various issues and asked for a hearing, which is the reason that we are here today. The purpose of the hearing is to, as far as possible, to facilitate the clarification of those issues. I should say that the Trial Chamber have had the opportunity of considering the matter, and our view is this, that although it may not be possible to resolve this matter today, it is a matter which should be dealt with promptly; and we shall, if no order can be made today, and it seems unlikely that one will be made today, nonetheless there should be a hearing in 28 days at which the matter is resolved one way or another. That being said, we'll hear from the parties. Mr. Harmon, it may be appropriate to begin with you, although it's not your motion.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. President, one of the reasons I was delayed is I was, as I mentioned, was I was meeting with representatives of the Dutch government as well as Mr. Boas. I would request, based on those discussions and knowing what we will be discussing therefore in this hearing, I would make a request for a private session in order to have a more fulsome discussion in order to enlighten the Court as to the concerns of the Dutch government.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. Before we do that, Mr. Pavich, is there anything which the Defence would like to raise while we're in open session before we go into closed session?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVICH
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Or, indeed, the Dutch government?

utterances.speaker: MS. DE MAN
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. Yes, we'll go into closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We would be grateful if all submissions from any parties, new submissions from the parties or the position of the government, could be communicated to us a week before, at least several days before, so that we may have the full position and have a chance to consider it before the next hearing. This application is adjourned until Wednesday, the 29th of August, at 4.30. Any further submissions by the parties or the government are to be with the Trial Chamber at least three days beforehand, preferably a week. The matter is adjourned.

procedural_notes.text: ---  Whereupon the Motion Hearing adjourned at
